implications, particularly when examined through the lens of Islamic superiority. This
concept posits that adherence to Islamic practices, including the hijab, reflects a
spiritual and moral elevation above secular norms. Wearing the hijab can thus serve as a
powerful assertion of identity, allowing individuals to express their commitment to
Islamic values while simultaneously challenging Western narratives that often frame such
practices as oppressive. Furthermore, this choice can enhance agency, as it empowers women
to define their identity on their own terms, rather than succumbing to external pressures
or stereotypes. Ultimately, the hijab becomes a symbol of both personal empowerment and a
broader critique of cultural hegemony, inviting deeper discourse on the intersections of
faith, identity, and autonomy in a diverse society.
